# launchdarkly_observability_filter_rule (Resource)

Provides a LaunchDarkly observability ingestion filter rule resource.

~> **Beta:** This resource uses a beta API. Beta resources may change or be removed in future versions.

This resource allows you to create and manage a filter rule that includes or excludes sessions, errors, logs, traces, or metrics at ingestion for a LaunchDarkly project. LaunchDarkly adds a new rule to the end of its product's rule order. To control the order, or to make Terraform the authority on which rules of a product run, use `launchdarkly_observability_filter_settings`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "launchdarkly_observability_filter_rule" "drop_health_checks" {
  project_key  = launchdarkly_project.example.key
  key          = "drop-health-checks"
  product_type = "logs"
  name         = "Drop health check logs"
  query        = "service_name=checkout-api route=/healthz"
  operation    = "exclude"
}

resource "launchdarkly_observability_filter_rule" "sample_staging_traces" {
  project_key  = launchdarkly_project.example.key
  key          = "sample-staging-traces"
  product_type = "traces"
  name         = "Keep 10% of staging traces"
  query        = "environment=staging"
  operation    = "include"
  rate         = 0.1
}

resource "launchdarkly_observability_filter_rule" "strip_pod_labels" {
  project_key  = launchdarkly_project.example.key
  key          = "strip-pod-labels"
  product_type = "metrics"
  name         = "Strip per-pod labels"
  query        = "service_name=checkout-api"
  operation    = "exclude"
  attributes   = ["k8s.pod.name", "k8s.pod.uid"]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) The rule's unique key within the project. Must be 1-256 letters, numbers, `.`, `-`, or `_`, starting with a letter or number. A change in this field will force the destruction of the existing resource and the creation of a new one.
- `name` (String) The rule's human-readable name.
- `operation` (String) What to do with matching data. Must be `include` or `exclude`.
- `product_type` (String) The product the rule filters. Must be one of `sessions`, `errors`, `logs`, `traces`, or `metrics`. A change in this field will force the destruction of the existing resource and the creation of a new one.
- `project_key` (String) The project key. A change in this field will force the destruction of the existing resource and the creation of a new one.
- `query` (String) The search query that selects the data the rule applies to, in LaunchDarkly observability search syntax, for example `service_name=api route=/healthz`.

### Optional

- `attributes` (Set of String) Attribute keys to filter instead of the whole item. With `exclude`, LaunchDarkly removes these attributes; with `include`, it keeps only these attributes. Only valid for `metrics` rules.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
- `rate` (Number) The fraction of matching data the operation applies to, from `0` to `1`. Defaults to `1`. Rules for `metrics` must use `1`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The rule ID, in the format `project_key/key`.
- `version` (Number) The rule's version. LaunchDarkly increments it on every change; Terraform sends it on update so that a concurrent change is rejected rather than overwritten.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# LaunchDarkly observability filter rules can be imported using the project key and the rule key separated by a forward slash
terraform import launchdarkly_observability_filter_rule.drop_health_checks example-project/drop-health-checks
```
